hypothesis.statement: The second pointer and the `base + i * 4` CSE are ONE lever and must be probed jointly. The target spends no callee-saved register on `base + i * 4`: it computes it into VOLATILE r4 for the first card store (`@0x100 add r4,r31,r27`, `@0x104 stw r3,64(r4)`, `@0x108 lwz r3,64(r4)`) and RECOMPUTES it for the foreground store into r22 -- the register `ent_h` has just vacated (`@0x140 add r22,r31,r27`, `@0x144 stw r3,80(r22)`, `@0x148 lwzu r3,80(r22)`). Ours CSEs the two groups into one callee-saved web (`@0x100 add r23,r31,r27` reused at `@0x140 stw r3,80(r23)`), which is exactly the register the second pointer needs. So the next lane adds `ent_h` AND defeats that CSE in the same probe, expecting `stmw r21,52(r1)` plus the `delete T[80:81]@140-144=['add']` cluster to close together. ONE SUCH JOINT PROBE WAS RUN HERE AND IS A NEGATIVE THE NEXT LANE MUST NOT REPEAT: `ent_h` at function scope together with `setupMapForeground((void**)((s32*)base + i), blit)` in place of `(void**)(base + i * 4)`. It DID split the web -- the `delete T[80:81]@140-144=['add']` cluster closed -- but the pointer-arithmetic transit is not free: it emitted its own `addi` (new cluster `insert T[64:64]@100-100=[] O[65:66]@104-108=['addi']`), taking insns to T185/O187, real 96, multiset 6t, and extabindex still MOVED. So the CSE break must come from a form that costs NO instruction of its own; the cast-transit no-CSE family's other members, and the TU's own `#pragma opt_common_subs` idiom (already used at line 1146, `reset`, so an `off`/`on` bracket is in-house style here) are the two untried directions.
